free_tier.stated: Up to USD 200 in Startup credits immediately to start building on Azure. Milestone 1 requires: sign up for Azure and verify your identity using a personal LinkedIn account, with no business accounts allowed at this step.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: USD 200 of Azure buys a few days of a small VM or a modest amount of Azure OpenAI usage. It composes as a way to test an Azure-only service before paying, and with the Azure free account allowance, but it is too small to train anything.

limits.value: USD 200 is the whole reachable slice; the next milestone is gated on business verification and everything above it on Azure spend a user does not have.

identity_cost.detail: A personal LinkedIn account plus an Azure signup.

evidence.proved: Milestone 1 is USD 200 and requires signing up for Azure and verifying identity with a personal LinkedIn account, quoted: 'Verify your identity (use a personal LinkedIn account, no business accounts allowed at this step)'
Milestone 2 is USD 5,000 and requires completing business verification, defined on the same page as 'Confirm your startup is a registered legal entity'
the full milestone ladder USD 200, USD 5,000, USD 25,000, USD 50,000, USD 150,000 with its workload and spend conditions, quoted
each 60-day clock starts once the workload count is met and every workload must stay above USD 1 of spend for all 60 days, quoted

notes: The program page itself, microsoft.com/en-us/startups, returns 200 but prints only marketing prose and no eligibility list; the Learn page carries the ladder. Treat USD 200 as the only part reachable without a legal entity. The one recorded is the better-evidenced.
